Rental car vs taxi in Tbilisi: the actual numbers

The choice between renting a car and living on Bolt is usually settled by preference. Below it is settled by arithmetic: fully loaded daily cost, the break-even point in trips per day, and the line item that never appears in a travel budget.

April 16, 2026 · Archi Rent

Defining the unit of comparison

A taxi has one cost line: the fare. A rental car has three, and only the first one appears on a price list. To compare like with like we use the fully loaded daily cost: daily rate plus fuel plus parking.

Base assumptions

Input Value
Economy class rate, 3–6 days 75 ₾ / day
Economy class rate, 7–29 days 68 ₾ / day
Business class rate, 3–6 days 210 ₾ / day
Fuel (60 km/day in town, hybrid) 12 ₾ / day
Paid parking in the centre 15 ₾ / day
Average Bolt city fare 11 ₾
Bolt, airport to centre 30 ₾ each way
Airport delivery of the car (3+ days) 0 ₾

On those inputs the fully loaded cost of an economy car is 75 + 12 + 15 = 102 GEL per day. For business class the same figure is 237 GEL.

The break-even point

The formula is straightforward: N = (daily rate + fuel + parking) ÷ average fare.

Economy class: 102 ÷ 11 ≈ 9 rides per day. Below nine movements a day, taxis are cheaper. Once you include the two airport transfers — which are free with a rental of three days or more — the threshold falls to roughly 7 or 8 rides.

Business class: 237 ÷ 20 (comfort-tier fare) ≈ 12 rides per day, which in practice only happens on a delegation schedule.

Three scenarios, costed

Scenario Taxi Rental Difference
3 days, 5 movements per day 225 ₾ 306 ₾ +81 ₾ against the rental
5 days, 8 movements plus one regional day 592 ₾ 538 ₾ −54 ₾ in favour of the rental
7 days, 8 movements per day 676 ₾ 665 ₾ −11 ₾, effectively a tie

Scenario 1 — short, city-centre visit. 3 × 5 × 11 = 165 GEL in town plus 60 GEL for airport transfers, so 225 GEL. The rental: 3 × 75 = 225, plus 36 fuel and 45 parking, so 306 GEL. Taxi wins.

Scenario 2 — an intensive week with a regional day. Four city days at eight movements come to 352 GEL, a day out to Rustavi and Mtskheta by taxi costs about 180 GEL, and airport transfers add 60 GEL: 592 GEL in total. The rental: 5 × 75 = 375, fuel over 440 km is 88, parking is 75 — 538 GEL. Rental wins.

Scenario 3 — a full week. From day seven the rate drops to 68 GEL and the two options land within a rounding error of each other. At that point the decision is no longer about price but about time.

The cost of waiting — the line item nobody budgets

Average wait from ordering to pick-up in Tbilisi runs 5 to 7 minutes, and longer at peak. Eight movements a day therefore consume roughly 45 to 50 minutes of working time.

If a manager's fully loaded cost to the company is 120 GEL an hour, that is 90 to 100 GEL a day of lost capacity. The 81 GEL advantage the taxi held in Scenario 1 disappears on that single line. This is precisely why companies keep choosing a car even when the spreadsheet shows taxis marginally ahead.

What neither column shows

On the rental side:

  • The deposit — 300 GEL on economy, 1,000 GEL on business class. It is blocked on the card rather than charged, and released within 3 business days of return. Treat it as a temporary use of working capital, not as an expense.
  • The excess — maximum exposure on damage is 300 to 1,200 GEL depending on category. SCDW takes it to zero for 25–45 GEL per day.
  • Traffic fines — at the renter's expense, plus 20 GEL processing, and they can arrive up to 30 days later.
  • Late return — free up to 2 hours, then one third of the daily rate for every 3 hours started.

On the taxi side:

  • surge pricing that lifts the average fare by 20–40% at exactly the moment you are late for a meeting;
  • unpredictable cost for any trip outside the city;
  • dozens of small receipts at month end, each one a separate line in an expense report.

That last point is often decisive for a finance team. With a rental you get one contract and one VAT invoice. Companies can pay by bank transfer, and on a corporate contract you receive a single monthly invoice plus a cost report broken down by vehicle.

When each option wins

Take taxis when:

  • the visit is one or two days and stays inside the centre;
  • you have fewer than five movements a day;
  • the evening involves alcohol;
  • parking at the hotel is unavailable or expensive.

Rent a car when:

  • the visit runs longer than three days on a dense schedule;
  • the plan includes Rustavi, Mtskheta, Kutaisi or a plant visit in the regions;
  • you travel as a group of three or four with luggage or demo equipment;
  • you need a predictable, pre-approved budget line;
  • movements happen after 22:00 or before 06:00.

A third option: a car with a driver, at 120 GEL per day for 8 hours on top of the business class, minivan or 4x4 rate. It is the most expensive column on paper, it reduces lost time to zero, and for a visiting delegation it is frequently the only defensible choice.

One rule worth stating plainly

Commercial use of a rental car — taxi work, Bolt, courier runs or haulage — is prohibited without prior written consent and voids the insurance cover. It is a common question and the answer is not negotiable.
